subject: Kickoff: QMon rollout for Aurora Payments — canary & rollback lanes
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@aurorapay.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: QMon rollout for Aurora Payments

Hi Aisha / Monica,

Thanks again for taking the time today. To summarize Aurora's priorities for the quality monitoring (QMon) rollout:
- Start with checkout/decline message flows and fraud-detection assistant outputs
- Prompt-sets: ~1,200 representative queries initially (mixture of English + es-ES)
- Integrate Redwood's eval harness into our staging pipeline; we can run nightly regression checks
- Canary windows: we want a low-risk first phase (1% traffic) and a staged increase if metrics look good

Immediate asks: could you send a quick staffing plan (who owns prompt curation, who owns eval automation) and a recommended canary/rollback matrix so our SREs can review? Also, we need to confirm logging/audit evidence for our internal compliance reviewers.

If helpful, Jenna (cc'd on follow-ups) is our product owner and will surface the internal test dataset.

Best,
Sam
Sam Patel
Director, Product Engineering
Aurora Payments

Attachments referenced: "customer-test-corpus_v1.zip" (we will upload to the Drive folder)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@aurorapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: QMon rollout for Aurora Payments

Thanks Sam — clear summary and great alignment on scope. I copied the initial playbook and two artifacts to get us moving: aurora_prompt_subset_v0.3.csv (small starter prompt set), canary_rollback_matrix.xlsx (recommended thresholds), and a short qmon-integration-checklist.pdf for the infra team. Links are in the Drive folder I shared.

High-level staffing and ownership (proposed):
- Prompt curation (owner): Monica Patel — curate baseline suite, manage updates from Aurora PO
- Eval harness integration (owner): Dylan Brooks — CI hooks, nightly runs, regression alerting on key metrics
- Canary orchestration + rollback policy (owner): Aisha Rahman — define windows and execute rollouts with SRE
- Security/compliance liaison: Rafael Mendes — readiness checks and artifact handoff

Timeline proposal (low-lift sequence):
1) Week 1 (this week): import prompt subset and run baseline eval on staging (1–2 days)
2) Week 2: integrate nightly regression runs + set initial alert thresholds (3–4 days)
3) Week 3: canary to 1% traffic for 48 hrs, evaluate metrics and increase to 5% if pass
4) Week 4: expand to full production traffic with continuous monitoring and automatic rollback triggers

Key knobs for agreement: metric names and pass criteria (we recommend: mean response latency, top-1 integrity score, hallucination rate proxy, and upstream error rate). I attached the starter CSV for prompt labeling and the canary matrix with suggested pass/fail bands.

Action items for Aurora: please drop the staging test corpus in the Drive folder and confirm your SRE contact so we can schedule a short runbook review.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a short internal checklist in the next email.

—Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: QMon rollout for Aurora Payments

Quick internal note on ownership and minimal runbook items — copying here so Aisha has it in one place.

Proposed staffing lanes (finalize by EOD Thursday):
- Prompt curation lane (Monica): ingest Aurora corpus, normalize aliases, flag high-risk prompts for manual review.
- Evaluation lane (Dylan): wire up Redwood eval harness to Aurora staging pipelines; implement nightly runs and a small 10-example smoke test before each deployment.
- Alerting lane (Marissa): implement regression alerting (PagerDuty + Slack), define page severity matrix.
- Canary lane (Aisha): escalate rollback plan and own rollouts.

Rollback policy (draft):
- Immediate rollback criteria (auto): >5% increase in hallucination proxy OR 300ms increase in p50 latency OR any functional errors that cause transaction failures.
- Investigate criteria (alert but no immediate rollback): upticks between 1–5% hallucination proxy OR isolated latency spikes.
- Manual hold: if external compliance raises audit concerns, hold rollout and run emergency audit checklist.

I'll draft the PD escalation rules and a short runbook section for the integration checklist. Please flag if any of the owners want to swap lanes.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior CS Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam@aurorapay.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Kline <jenna@aurorapay.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: QMon rollout for Aurora Payments

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Couple clarifications from our side:
- Our compliance team will want evidence of data retention and audit logs for the eval harness runs (timestamps + config). Rafael is our internal security lead (I copied him). Can Redwood provide a short artifact pack?
- On rollback thresholds: Aurora prefers a conservative auto-rollback on any transaction-affecting errors; for quality metrics (hallucination proxy), can we start with a stricter initial band (auto rollback at >3%) and then relax to 5% after two successful canary windows?
- Also confirm whether the eval harness can tag examples with both model-version and quantization profile so we can map regressions to specific model variants.

If you can reply with a brief confirmation on the above, we can lock the SRE review time.

Thanks,
Sam

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@aurorapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff: QMon rollout for Aurora Payments — canary & rollback lanes

Sam — quick confirmations and next steps:

1) Audit artifacts: Rafael and team, we will produce a QMon artifact bundle (s3://redwood-aurora/qmon-artifacts/2027-06-05/) that contains eval run metadata (timestamps, model+quantization tags), config used for each run, and hashed test inputs so Aurora compliance can verify without ingesting PII. Rafael will coordinate exact format.

2) Canary thresholds: happy to accommodate Aurora's conservative start. We will use the following sequence: 1% traffic (48 hrs) with auto-rollback at >3% hallucination proxy OR transaction failures; if pass, move to 5% (72 hrs) with auto-rollback at >5% OR >300ms p50 increase; then consider staged ramp to 25%/100% with agreed gating. See attached canary_rollback_matrix.xlsx for bands.

3) Eval harness tags: Dylan confirms the harness already records model_version and quant_profile metadata per example. We'll include this in the artifact bundle and in the regression alert payloads so you can filter by variant.

4) SRE runbook review: propose Tue 06/08 09:30 PT for a 30-min runbook walkthrough (I'll send the calendar invite once Jenna confirms).

Action items captured:
- Aurora: upload staging corpus to Drive folder (Jenna)
- Redwood: finalize artifact bundle format (Rafael), wire nightly regression to Aurora staging (Dylan), lock staffing lanes (Monica/Marissa)
- Schedule runbook review (Aisha)

Thanks everyone — I'll track these in HubSpot (HS-973452) and update the Drive folder with the artifacts and the SOW link.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments included: aurora_prompt_subset_v0.3.csv, canary_rollback_matrix.xlsx, qmon-integration-checklist.pdf
